summary: Toshio Horiuchi works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2003–2009) and held posts at Toyo University (~2012–2018) and Zhejiang University (~2018).

Toshio Nagahiro specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there as a professor (~1950–1969), held posts at its Institute for Research in Humanities, and was president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

Toshio Sako is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University under his doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1977), Chuo University (~1977–1987), Tokyo Institute of Technology, and Hannan University.

Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. Unebe served as an associate professor in Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2006–2011).

Totsudo Kato worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Bankon Shimada at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University, later teaching at Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Touhoi Fok was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, Otani University, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, where he served as a lecturer (~1972–1999).

Touraj Daryaee is an Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology scholar. He completed his studies at UCLA in 1999 and took up a post at the University of California, Irvine, around 2007.

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his degrees at Kyoto University. He taught at Otemon Gakuin University, served as a professor at Osaka City University, and was director of the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).
Traian Costa was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Vlad Bănățeanu. He served as a professor teaching Sanskrit at the University of Bucharest in 1963.

Trang T. D. Nguyen works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ho Chi Minh City Open University, the University of South Wales, and the University of Vienna, and held roles including regional coordinator at Play for Peace.

Travis L. Smith works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and completed his PhD at Columbia University under John Stratton Hawley, later holding posts at Barnard College, the University of Florida, and UC Berkeley.
Trent Walker works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, under the supervision of Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology, studying at King's College London and SOAS under Hari Prasad Shastri, Arthur Waley, and Yukio Tani. He headed the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) and lectured for the Buddhist Society.

Trevor Ling was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Leeds (1963–1972) and the University of Manchester (1972–1982), among other institutions.

Trijang Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Gyuto Monastery and under masters including Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo. He succeeded Ling Rinpoche and taught prominent students, including the 14th Dalai Lama.

Trine Brox specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at UiT and the University of Copenhagen, where Christian K. Wedemeyer supervised her MA, and has held teaching positions at Copenhagen, including associate professor in 2014.
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tro Shul Khenpo Jampal Dorjé studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Parsons College, the University of Akron, Ohio University, and Chatham University (~1954–1964).
